videos.title: Ile pieniędzy trzeba mieć, żeby nie pracować? Policzyłem
videos.description:
Ile pieniędzy wystarczy do końca życia? Liczę to trzema sposobami: wydatki razy lata, reguła 4% i symulacja z ZUS i zyskiem 3% ponad inflację. W przykładzie czteroosobowej rodziny wychodzi od 2,41 do 5,64 mln zł, zależnie od założeń.

Osiągnąłem wolność finansową w wieku około 35 lat. Dalej prowadziłem firmę i wynosiłem śmieci. Dziś wciąż noszę telefon z zepsutym gniazdem. Opowiadam, skąd się bierze ten odruch i jak by wyglądał mój zwykły wtorek, gdybym miał już wystarczająco.

videos.title: Pobór do wojska to niewolnictwo. Kto obroni Polskę? - Mikołaj Pisarski | Finansowy Preppers
videos.description:
Czy powrót do obowiązkowego poboru do wojska zwiększy bezpieczeństwo Polski, czy wygeneruje gigantyczne koszty gospodarcze i społeczne? Mikołaj Pisarski w rozmowie z Jackiem Jakubiukiem analizuje propozycje powszechnego poboru z perspektywy wolnościowej i ekonomicznej. Dlaczego przymusowa służba wojskowa jest w istocie niesprawiedliwym podatkiem płaconym w naturze, nałożonym wyłącznie na najmłodsze roczniki?

W wywiadzie padają konkretne liczby i porównania międzynarodowe. Polska już teraz w ramach dobrowolnej zasadniczej służby wojskowej szkoli ponad 40 000 rekrutów rocznie - to więcej niż wynosi cały roczny pobór w Finlandii (nieco ponad 20 000), która jest w debacie publicznej stawiana za główny wzór. Kluczowym problemem pozostaje jednak brak oficjalnej, opublikowanej strategii obrony państwa polskiego, bez której niemożliwe jest rzetelne oszacowanie realnych potrzeb kadrowych i sprzętowych.

Rozmowa schodzi również na temat wniosków z wojny na Ukrainie, przymusu demotywującego żołnierzy, a także kondycji polskiej gospodarki, w której sektor publiczny wypiera prywatną przedsiębiorczość. Mikołaj Pisarski podsumowuje także pierwsze efekty reform wolnorynkowych i deregulacji rządu Javiera Milei w Argentynie.

videos.title: Jak zacząć inwestować w nieruchomości bez MILIONÓW? | Maciej Kubik
videos.description:
Maciej Kubik jest przedsiębiorcą z Krakowa i od lat działa na rynku nieruchomości. Zbudował biuro wyspecjalizowane w sprzedaży działek, robił flipy i projekty deweloperskie, a dziś razem ze wspólnikiem udziela przedsiębiorcom pożyczek pod zastaw nieruchomości. Wspólnika poznał w ASBiRO, gdzie sam zaczynał od kursów dla przedsiębiorców.

To rozmowa dla osób, które chcą zacząć inwestować w nieruchomości bez milionów na koncie, i dla przedsiębiorców, którzy dostają propozycje wspólnych inwestycji.

Z tego wywiadu dowiesz się:

➡️ Na co wydałby 100 tysięcy złotych, a na co 500 tysięcy, gdyby zaczynał dziś?

videos.title: Co naprawdę wspiera rozwój psychiczny niemowlęcia
videos.description:
[współpraca barterowa] Materiał zawiera segment reklamowy mleka Laktowit 2, przeznaczonego dla niemowląt po 6. miesiącu życia*
Link do reklamowanego produktu: https://laktowit.pl

*Karmienie piersią jest najlepszym sposobem żywienia niemowląt. Mleko następne jest przeznaczone dla niemowląt po 6. miesiącu życia jako część zróżnicowanej diety; nie zastępuje mleka kobiecego w pierwszych sześciu miesiącach. Decyzje dotyczące żywienia dziecka warto podejmować przy wsparciu osoby mającej odpowiednie kwalifikacje.

Co naprawdę wpływa na rozwój psychiczny i emocjonalny niemowlęcia? Czy reagowaniem na płacz można „rozpieścić” dziecko? Jakie znaczenie mają bezpieczna więź, przytulanie, sen, odżywianie i zdrowie psychiczne rodziców?
W tym odcinku wyjaśniam prostym językiem, co wiemy z badań o pierwszym roku życia, ze szczególnym uwzględnieniem pierwszych sześciu miesięcy.
Porozmawiamy o:
• budowaniu bezpiecznej relacji z opiekunami;
• reagowaniu na płacz i rozpoznawaniu potrzeb;
• bliskości i kontakcie skóra do skóry;
• codziennej komunikacji wspierającej rozwój;
• roli snu i zasadach bezpiecznego spania;
• żywieniu niemowląt;
• dobrostanie psychicznym rodziców;
• mitach, które dokładają rodzinom niepotrzebnej presji.

Oddzielam zalecenia od wyników pojedynczych badań i zaznaczam granice naszej wiedzy.


Materiał ma charakter edukacyjny i nie zastępuje indywidualnej oceny zdrowia ani rozwoju dziecka.

videos.title: Why Men Don't Have FRIENDS Anymore
videos.description:
Why men don't have friends anymore: if you're losing friends as you get older, scroll to the bottom of your texts. There's a name down there you used to talk to every day.
Here are the 5 reasons male friendship fades after 40, why so many men end up lonely, and how to make friends as an adult again, starting with one call this Thanksgiving.
📌 Why MEN Over 60 CUT EVERYONE OFF | Psychology Explained: https://youtu.be/jKN6mFPZ-QU

Most men don't lose their friends in a fight. Life gets full with marriage, kids and work, and a lot of dads feel guilty taking time for friends. Work friends go quiet the day you change jobs or retire. Moving to a new city turns a 10-minute drive into a 3-hour one. Men make friends side by side, so when the softball team or the fishing trip ends, the friendship loses its reason. And nobody makes the first call, so old friends slowly disappear. In 1990, 3% of men said they had no close friends. In 2021 it was 15%.

Remi explains what "too late" really looks like, what to do when an old friend calls you, and how wives and partners can help. Then the good news: how to call an old friend again (start with a memory), how to keep friends once you do (a monthly breakfast, be the one who sends the text), and how to make new friends after 40 if it feels like you have no friends left.

Who's the one friend you're calling this Thanksgiving? Just his first name, below.

videos.description:
📌 Dołącz do nas w mentoringu Zjednoczenie:
https://wysokie-wibracje.pl/zjednoczenie/

Jak być spokojem, kiedy właśnie przyszedł kolejny rachunek?
Jak być miłością, kiedy od dawna brakuje Ci bliskości?
Jak być obfitością, kiedy stan konta wciąż mówi co innego?

To trzecie i ostatnie spotkanie z cyklu „Droga do Zjednoczenia siebie”. Rozmawiamy w nim o tym, co dzieje się, kiedy już wiesz, kim chcesz być, a Twoje życie na razie wygląda tak samo jak wczoraj.

I od razu dobra wiadomość: utrzymanie stanu spełnionego pragnienia nie polega na tym, żeby codziennie budzić się w euforii, nigdy nie czuć lęku i nigdy nie wątpić. Polega na czymś dużo spokojniejszym i dużo bardziej realnym.

🎻 Kiedy jeden instrument w orkiestrze odzywa się głośniej, muzyka nie przestaje grać. Dyrygent nadal prowadzi.
💞 Para, która jest razem od dwudziestu lat, nie budzi się co rano zachwycona, że jest kochana. A jednak wie, że miłość jest częścią jej życia.
🧾 Niespodziewany rachunek to problem do rozwiązania, a nie wyrok na całą Twoją przyszłość.

W tym LIVE:
✨ dlaczego stan JESTEM to nie emocja, tylko punkt odniesienia, do którego wracasz
✨ czym różni się emocja, założenie i stan JESTEM
✨ 4 powody, dla których życie z wybranego JESTEM daje więcej energii i sprawczości
✨ jak poczuć coś, czego jeszcze nie przeżyłaś ani nie przeżyłeś (podpowiedź: znasz już jakości, z których to się składa)
✨ patrzenie NA pragnienie a patrzenie Z jego spełnienia
✨ dlaczego lepiej wyobrazić sobie zwyczajny wtorek niż wielki moment triumfu
✨ co robić, kiedy rzeczywistość przeczy Twojemu nowemu JESTEM
✨ ćwiczenie: nazwij swoje JESTEM i znajdź trzy dowody z własnego życia, że już znasz ten stan
✨ zadanie na trzy wieczory: zasypianie w nowym JESTEM
✨ pytania i odpowiedzi na żywo

Przygotuj notatnik i coś do pisania. Ćwiczenie robisz razem z nami.

„Utrzymanie nowego JESTEM nie polega na tym, że nigdy nie wracasz do dawnych emocji. Polega na tym, że coraz rzadziej wracasz do dawnych wniosków na swój temat.”

Can you make a living from open source? Ronald Dehuysser does. He created JobRunr, a Java library for background job processing, and went from €0 to €80,000 in revenue in six months, after two and a half years working on it in his spare time.

videos.title: Wybieram, ile chcę zarabiać | Świadomy rytuał finansowej wolności [432Hz]
videos.description:
ARCHITEKTURA DOSTATKU | Świadomy rytuał finansowej wolności

🎧 POSŁUCHAJ TAKŻE:

✨ [https://youtu.be/lPrSuCuXIRw](https://youtu.be/lPrSuCuXIRw)

✨ [https://youtu.be/UOcBfVuBegc](https://youtu.be/UOcBfVuBegc)

A gdybyś to Ty decydowała, ile chcesz zarabiać każdego miesiąca?

Nie według cudzych oczekiwań. Nie według dawnych ograniczeń. Według własnych potrzeb, pragnień i wizji życia w dostatku.

Śpiewane afirmacje na obfitość finansową to zaproszenie do świadomego określenia własnych celów finansowych, budowania poczucia bezpieczeństwa i otwarcia się na większy dobrobyt.

Architektura dostatku to wyjątkowy rytuał finansowej wolności, który łączy śpiewane afirmacje obfitości, dostatku i wewnętrznego spokoju. Nie narzuca Ci konkretnej sumy. To Ty świadomie wybierasz swoją miesięczną kwotę — taką, która oznacza dla Ciebie bezpieczeństwo, niezależność i większą swobodę życia.

Nagranie łączy dwa uzupełniające się utwory afirmacyjne.

✨ CZĘŚĆ 1 – Moja wybrana obfitość

Świadomie określasz swoją miesięczną kwotę. Wzmacniasz poczucie własnej wartości, sprawczości i prawa do finansowego dobrobytu. Uczysz się myśleć o swoich możliwościach bez ograniczania ich dawnymi przekonaniami.

✨ CZĘŚĆ 2 – Spokój i naturalny przepływ

Uwalniasz napięcie związane z pieniędzmi, oswajasz lęk przed brakiem i otwierasz się na nowe możliwości. Łączysz pragnienie większych dochodów z poczuciem bezpieczeństwa, spokojem i zaufaniem do własnych decyzji.

💛 JAK KORZYSTAĆ Z TEGO RYTUAŁU?

1. Wybierz swoją miesięczną kwotę.

Zastanów się, ile naprawdę chcesz zarabiać każdego miesiąca. Pozwól sobie wybrać konkretną sumę, która odpowiada Twoim potrzebom i aspiracjom.

2. Włącz swoją intencję do refrenu.

Kiedy usłyszysz słowa o wyborze nowej miesięcznej normy finansowej, wypowiedz na głos lub w myślach własną kwotę.

Nie musisz nikomu jej ujawniać. To Twoja osobista decyzja.

3. Słuchaj z uważnością.

Możesz wracać do tych afirmacji rano, wieczorem lub wtedy, gdy potrzebujesz przypomnieć sobie o własnej wartości i możliwościach.

Zauważaj swoje przekonania dotyczące pieniędzy. Łącz afirmacje ze świadomymi wyborami i działaniami, które wspierają Twoje cele finansowe.

Nie chodzi o to, by uzależniać swoje szczęście od konkretnej sumy. Chodzi o możliwość samodzielnego określenia, czym jest dla Ciebie dostatek, i budowania życia w zgodzie z własnymi wartościami.

Mam prawo pragnąć więcej. Mam prawo żyć spokojnie. Mam prawo sama określać swoje finansowe cele . 

Niech te słowa staną się Twoją osobi

videos.title: Ile naprawdę ZARABIA TRENER personalny? | Marcin Rybak
videos.description:
Branża fitness kusi dużymi zarobkami. Ale co zostaje, gdy trzeba zdobyć pierwszych podopiecznych, opłacić karnet trenerski i poradzić sobie z odwołanymi treningami? Marcin Rybak opowiada, jak wygląda praca trenera personalnego po ponad 10 latach w zawodzie.

W podcaście Akademii Szkolenia Trenerów Maksymilian Furtak pyta o pieniądze, błędy początkujących i granicę między dobrym marketingiem a rzeczywistymi kompetencjami. Rozmawiamy o tym, dlaczego świetna sylwetka nie gwarantuje pełnego grafiku, czy krótki kurs wystarczy na start i jak budować współpracę, która trwa latami.

Marcin wyjaśnia, dlaczego zrezygnował z pomysłu własnego studia, jak ustala zasady odwoływania treningów i co zmienił w swoim podejściu do podopiecznych. Jest też o niepotrzebnym komplikowaniu ćwiczeń, nachalnej sprzedaży oraz historii podopiecznego, który schudł około 37 kg.

Ile można zarobić na treningach personalnych, a ile dzięki działalności w social mediach? Oddzielamy te dwa modele pracy. Podawane kwoty to szacunki gościa dla określonych warunków, a nie gwarancja zarobków po kursie.

Myślisz o zawodzie trenera albo już pracujesz na siłowni? Posłuchaj, zanim oprzesz swój plan wyłącznie na historiach sukcesu.

👉 Sprawdź kursy i szkolenia AST: https://ast.edu.pl/
💬 Co najbardziej zaskoczyło Cię w pracy trenera? Napisz w komentarzu.
🔔 Subskrybuj kanał AST, żeby nie przegapić kolejnych rozmów.

videos.description:
In the final part of his conversation with Sam, former MLB closer Cody Allen talks about something many men feel and few say out loud: loneliness. For 34 years he was 99% known, and he says that is the same as being unknown. Shame keeps us at a distance, and a podcast or a Sunday sermon can start to feel like enough. But honesty costs nothing. Vulnerability costs something, and that is where freedom is found. The answer to the male loneliness epidemic isn't more content. It's belonging to the body, serving alongside other men, and refusing to live on the fringe.

Cody also shares how he hopes to be remembered: as a steady presence who shields his family from the waves. And he tells us who he is without baseball, a man deeply in love with the Lord, faithfully and clumsily trying to abide. He describes Scripture as a box of letters from a Father who loves us. And he remembers the night the Jesus Storybook Bible brought him to tears in front of his sons. The deepest cost of the cross wasn't the nails. It was distance from the Father, carried so we would never have to know it.

We pray this message will encourage, challenge, and transform. As always, we invite you to share it with someone who needs it.

videos.title: Why Some People Live Inside Their Minds More Than In Real Life
videos.description:
Metacognition is the ability to think about your own thinking, allowing you to observe, understand, and regulate your internal mental processes.

But what happens when you become so deeply aware of your own thoughts that you start living more inside your mind than in the world around you?

We often find ourselves questioning our decisions, analyzing every possible outcome, and replaying memories from the past. This video explores the psychology behind these patterns, including Analysis Paralysis and Rumination, and how excessive thinking can sometimes prevent us from experiencing the present moment.

Through the philosophy of Søren Kierkegaard, we explore the anxiety of endless possibilities, the importance of making choices, and what it truly means to live in the present.

I also share my personal experiences with overthinking, self-awareness, and the realization that changed the way I look at time, decisions, and my own future.

Understanding your mind is a powerful tool for personal growth, but understanding alone isn't always enough. Sometimes, the most meaningful changes begin when we stop imagining every possible future and start taking small, consistent steps toward the life we want to live.

Your thoughts can show you a thousand different possibilities, but only your actions can turn one of them into reality.

Spread vision with Berkay ⟢

videos.title: Every Level of Male Loneliness (Most Men Are Stuck at Level 3)
videos.description:
Most men spend their entire lives stuck on level three of loneliness without ever realizing there's anything above it.

This video walks through seven levels of male loneliness — from choosing to be alone, to drifting from friends, to the trap most men never notice they're in, all the way to becoming someone who is present when there and unmissed when gone.

You'll meet the researchers behind each level: Louise Hawkley on solitude vs. loneliness, Robin Dunbar on social network layers, social baseline theory from Marta Zarzycki and James Coan, Mark Granovetter on weak ties, Stephanie Spielman on the fear of being alone, Julianne Holt-Lunstad on isolation and health, and Ami Rokach on chronic loneliness.

Ask yourself at the end: at which level are you — really?

WATCH NEXT
The Psychology of Men Who Have No Close Friends
[link to relevant existing video]

When did you first notice your circle getting smaller — was it a moment, or did it just happen? Share your experience in the comments.

Subscribe to Inside Your Thinking for psychology behind everyday behavior and relationships.

FURTHER READING
These sources provide background and important context; they do not establish every interpretation in the narration.

Louise C. Hawkley and colleagues — research on loneliness as perceived social isolation, distinct from objective alone-ness (University of Chicago).

Robin Dunbar — social network layers and the approximate size of the inner close-relationship circle (Oxford University).

Marta S. Bernstein (Beckes) and James L. Coan — Social Baseline Theory: the brain expects proximity to trusted others and uses it to reduce regulatory effort (University of Virginia).

Mark S. Granovetter — "The Strength of Weak Ties" (American Journal of Sociology, 1973): casual connections as carriers of opportunity and wider belonging (Stanford).

Stephanie Spielman and colleagues — research on the fear of being single and its effects on relationship choices.

Julianne Holt-Lunstad and colleagues — meta-analytic work on social isolation, loneliness, and health risk (Brigham Young University).

Ami Rokach — work on loneliness as a phenomenon that can become chronic and self-reinforcing.

Important context: both social isolation and loneliness have been associated with health risks in the research literature. Choosing time alone is not the same as establishing that social isolation is harmless.

videos.title: Analysis Paralysis: Why Thinking Harder Keeps You Stuck
videos.description:
Have you ever spent so much time thinking about a decision that you ended up making no decision at all?
You research your options, consider the consequences, and try to figure out which choice is best. But instead of becoming clearer, the decision seems to get more complicated.
Why does that happen? And why doesn't thinking harder always help?
In this MindLit Labs conversation, we explore analysis paralysis and the psychology behind our difficulty making decisions. We'll consider how loss aversion, fear of regret, and competing desires can keep us stuck, even when we know what we want.
We'll also examine an interesting biblical perspective on being divided within ourselves, drawing from 1 Kings 18 and the book of James.
But there's a practical question worth considering: What if the difficulty you're experiencing isn't simply a lack of information? What if there's something about the decision itself that you haven't fully come to terms with?
Together, we'll explore how to recognize what's holding you back, evaluate the potential cost of your choices, and move beyond indecision without assuming that moving forward always means saying yes.
If you've been struggling with a difficult decision, or find yourself caught in a cycle of overthinking, this conversation may help you see your situation a little differently.

videos.title: Know What To Do But Can't Act? Here Is Why
videos.description:
#Psychology #OvercomeProcrastination #CognitivePulse 
Do you know exactly what you need to do, but find yourself completely paralyzed? Discover why you can't take action and how your brain is secretly protecting you.
If you are lying awake at 2 AM calling yourself lazy or useless, you are entirely misunderstanding your own mind. The psychology of inaction isn't about a lack of willpower, discipline, or drive; it is a highly systemic defense mechanism. When you constantly ask yourself why you can't take action, the answer usually lies in self-handicapping—a subconscious behavioral strategy where you avoid giving 100% effort because you are terrified of finding out your true limits.
In this video, we dive deep into the behavioral psychology behind why smart, high-potential people often find themselves feeling stuck in a survival loop. We break down the science of why you escape into your phone for seven hours a day to avoid the silence, and why that late-night guilt trip is actually a fake psychological punishment that stops you from making real changes. By understanding these cognitive traps and the hidden fear of failure, you can finally uncover exactly why you can't take action and learn how to permanently overcome procrastination without self-loathing.
⏱️ TIMESTAMPS / KEY CHAPTERS: 
00:00 - The Real Reason Why You Can't Take Action 
01:30 - The Self-Handicapping Pill: Fear of Your Own Limits 
02:30 - The Curse of "Having So Much Potential" 
03:30 - Screen Time vs. Silence: Escaping Your Thoughts 
04:30 - The 1 AM Guilt Trip (Fake Psychological Punishment) 
05:30 - Redesign Your System: How to Overcome Procrastination 
07:30 - Breaking the Survival Loop
🧠 SCIENTIFIC PRACTICE (AT-HOME RESOURCE): You cannot change your nervous system simply by thinking differently, aggressively judging yourself, or forcing sheer willpower. You need to redesign your behavioral system. One of the safest and most effective methods based on behavioral psychology is the "5-Minute Action Shrink."
You can start applying this today by breaking down massive, paralyzing life plans into one single micro-task that takes exactly 5 minutes (e.g., writing one terrible sentence, sending one short email, or organizing one folder). Set a timer, start moving, and give yourself full permission to stop when it rings. Action precedes motivation—by removing the pressure of the outcome, you teach your brain that it is safe to start without needing to feel "ready."
#Psychology #OvercomeProcrastinat

videos.title: Dopóki nie zmierzysz się ze swoim cieniem, on cię zniszczy – Carl Jung
videos.description:
Co jeśli ciemność, której boisz się najbardziej, od zawsze żyje w tobie? Wiele osób uważa się za spokojnych, dobrych i pełnych empatii, nie zdając sobie sprawy, że za tą fasadą kryje się niebezpieczna iluzja. Zostań do końca, aby odkryć, jak odzyskać pełną kontrolę nad własnym losem.

Carl Jung nazwał tę ukrytą, instynktowną stronę naszej psychiki cieniem. Im bardziej ją ignorujesz i spychasz w głąb podświadomości, tym większą władzę nad tobą przejmuje. Niewytłumaczalne wybuchy gniewu, nagła irytacja na zachowanie innych, zazdrość czy ciągły autosabotaż w najważniejszych momentach życia to wyraźne sygnały, że to nie ty trzymasz stery. Wszystko, czego nie chcesz w sobie zaakceptować, zaczyna kierować twoimi decyzjami, a ty nazywasz to pechem lub przeznaczeniem.

Prawdziwa wolność rodzi się dopiero wtedy, gdy odważysz się spojrzeć w oczy swojej mrocznej stronie i w pełni ją zintegrować. Obejrzyj ten materiał do ostatniej minuty i napisz w komentarzu, jaką część swojego cienia najtrudniej ci zaakceptować. Jakie emocje lub impulsy ukrywasz nawet przed samym sobą?

#Psychologia #RozwójOsobisty #Samopoznanie #Filozofia #Umysł #Świadomość #Podświadomość #CarlJung #Cień #PracaZCieniem #Autosabotaż #Emocje #PsychologiaGłębi #WewnętrznaWolność #IntegracjaCienia

videos.title: Men, Loneliness & The Need For Real Friends
videos.description:
Why are so many men lonelier than ever? In this episode of What Makes This Make Sense?, Capstone Wellness therapists Jimmy Shaw and Jeremy Carter look at the steep decline in close male friendships and ask what’s really behind it, and what it would take to get those friendships back.

Jimmy and Jeremy explore how shifting expectations at home have squeezed the time men once had for friends, why staying in so often feels easier than showing up, and how self-care and self-optimization can quietly turn into isolation.

From the idea of a “social battery” that can’t be recharged to online spaces that turn other men into competition, they look at how a culture focused on becoming our best selves may be leaving us to do it alone. The good news is that connection can be rebuilt, often in simple ways.

They talk about why men tend to connect best side by side rather than face to face, the value of unstructured time around a campfire, a card table, or a weekly breakfast, and why asking a friend for help can be a gift to both of you. They also ask a question every man should be able to answer: who’s your 2 a.m. Call?

Plus: things that don’t make sense, from drive-through trick-or-treating to four-way stops.

The good news is that connection can be rebuilt, one small step at a time. Nobody plans to end up without close friends. The conversation is about understanding how it happens, and how to start reaching out.

www.capstonewellness.com

videos.title: Kto Nie Docenił Twojej Obecności, Zrozumie Twoją Wartość Dopiero W Twojej Nieobecności | Carl Jung
videos.description:
Zniknij na chwilę w ciszy i zobacz, co odkrył Carl Jung o prawie świadomego wycofania, dzięki któremu Twoja podświadomość i nieświadomość odzyskują utraconą siłę. Psychologia głębi wyjaśnia, dlaczego stała dostępność dla innych odbiera Ci własny spokój.

Żyjemy w świecie, który uczynił ze stałej dostępności najwyższy obowiązek. Odpisujesz od razu, odbierasz każdy telefon, bierzesz na siebie cudze sprawy — aż pewnego dnia odkrywasz, że chociaż jesteś nieustannie obecny w życiu dziesiątek ludzi, całkowicie zniknąłeś z życia własnego. Carl Gustav Jung przypominał, że nie da się odzyskać własnej duszy pośród ciągłego hałasu.

W tym nagraniu odkryjesz, dlaczego ciągła dostępność wypłukuje Cię z wewnętrznej siły, jak stworzyć własną nienaruszalną przestrzeń ciszy bez poczucia winy i jak wrócić między ludzi na własnych warunkach.

videos.description:
Why can saying two simple letters — NO — make us feel guilty?

You know you have the right to refuse. You may be exhausted, busy, or simply unwilling to agree. Yet you still worry about disappointing someone, appearing selfish, or damaging a relationship.

In this video, we explore the psychology behind guilt, people-pleasing, social expectations, and the emotional difficulty of setting boundaries.

We also look at an important distinction: feeling guilty because you’ve done something wrong is not the same as feeling guilty because someone didn’t get what they wanted.

Jensen Huang was forced out of the company he co-founded over an affair. But Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos had affairs too, and they kept running Microsoft and Amazon. So why did Huang pay such a high price? Economist Steve Keen argues the affair was the excuse, not the reason.

In this video, Steve looks at the bigger fight behind Huang's exit: America's battle with China over AI. Huang wanted to sell Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies and data centres, and he backed the open-source approach to AI that Chinese companies have taken, while America's biggest AI companies keep their models closed. Steve argues that this put him on the wrong side of Washington and of US big tech, and that trying to remove him won't stop China.

He also explains why Nvidia matters so much in the first place: how artificial intelligence actually works, why it needs GPUs instead of ordinary computer chips, why that means enormous, power-hungry data centres, and why China's power system gives it a major advantage in the AI race.

Get the free weekly market brief, read by 9,000+ investors: https://onchainmind.io/brief

Is this Bitcoin capitulation? In this video I measure it in dollars rather than coins: almost 80% of all the money invested in Bitcoin is now underwater, up from 42% in September and close to the 87% of the June low. Every major cycle bottom since 2011 came with 88% to 98% of dollars underwater, and half of all the money only gets back to break even at about $81,600.

We dig into who actually sold, using the new Who Cashed In view: the newest buyers and the people who bought near the top, selling at more than three times their usual pace, while holders of three years and more kept trickling out profit at their normal rate. Then the forced selling: $1.8 billion of long liquidations in a week, the new Wipeout Rank at Historic wipeout, and almost 11% of open interest flushed out.

videos.title: The Masculine Routine
videos.description:
Find your philosophy. Then live it. → https://studio.com/bygone-philosophy

"There is no more miserable human being than one in whom nothing is habitual but indecision." William James wrote that in 1890. This film is about the opposite man: the one whose day is not negotiated but designed. It follows Anthony Trollope, a careless junior clerk at the Post Office who, by writing every morning from half past five, produced forty-seven novels alongside a full career, and then walks the whole path of a strong man's day, from the hour he rises to the hour he sleeps.

Millions of men are stepping away from dating, marriage, homeownership, and traditional provider roles. But what happens when men stop spending money on the life they were expected to build?

From collapsing dating expectations and declining marriage rates to falling college enrollment, delayed homeownership, and changing consumer spending, the traditional American Dream is being rewritten.

videos.description:
Who owns the most of America's $40 trillion debt? China? Japan? Neither. The biggest foreign lender may actually be a tiny group of islands in the Caribbean. So how did the Cayman Islands end up lending America more money than either of them?

China has cut its Treasury holdings by more than half, while hedge funds in the Cayman Islands are borrowing huge amounts of money to buy American bonds. Meanwhile, Social Security, the Federal Reserve, and even crypto companies are lending Washington money.

In this video, I explain who really owns America's debt, how risky bond trades and rising interest payments could put pressure on the system, and why the biggest threat to America's ability to repay its lenders may come from Congress itself.

videos.title: Why Erika Kirk Feels "Off" to Everyone — It's Not What You Think
videos.description:
Why does Erika Kirk feel "off" to so many viewers — unsettling rather than sympathetic — even when her words sound right?

As a gay male therapist in West Hollywood, I break down the disconnect between Erika Kirk's words, facial expressions, and emotional presentation in her interviews and memorial speech, and why that mismatch polarizes people.

Drawing on Nancy McWilliams's Psychoanalytic Diagnosis, I explore three concepts associated with antisocial personality dynamics:

1. Emotion as an instrument rather than an expression — when emotional language seems designed to influence others rather than communicate genuine feeling.
2. Omnipotent control — how power, dominance, and tight narrative control can make emotional appeals function as tools of influence.
3. Affect Incongruence — why incongruence between words and nonverbal communication can provoke distrust and a feeling of being managed, not moved.

I also look at why media narratives cannot simply override our automatic emotional responses, and why we should trust our instincts enough to investigate them — not as a verdict, but as a signal.

This isn't about diagnosing Erika Kirk from a distance or claiming to know whether her grief is genuine. It's a psychoanalytic framework for understanding why her public presentation generates such polarized reactions — and what grief, dissociation, media coaching, and compartmentalization can and can't explain.

Let me know in the comments: when you watch her, do you feel moved, managed, or both? And what moment made you feel that way?

videos.title: Don't Stop Buying Dividends in a Crash Until You See This Math
videos.description:
Don't Stop Buying Dividends in a Crash Until You See This Math

What happens when the stock market crashes while you're building a dividend portfolio? Should you stop investing, wait for the market to recover, or keep buying dividend stocks and ETFs while prices are falling?

In this video, we break down the math behind dividend investing during a stock market crash—and why continuing to invest through market downturns could make a major difference in your long-term wealth.

When stock prices fall, many investors panic and stop buying. But for long-term dividend investors, lower share prices can create opportunities to accumulate more shares with the same amount of money. And if dividends remain stable, those additional shares could generate more dividend income over time.

We'll explore what happens when you continue investing $500 or $1,000 per month during a market crash, how dividend reinvestment works when prices decline, and why dollar-cost averaging can be a powerful strategy for building long-term wealth.

We'll also examine how dividend ETFs like SCHD, DGRO, and VYM may behave during market downturns, the relationship between falling stock prices and dividend yields, and how dividend growth and compound interest can affect your portfolio's recovery.

Can buying dividend ETFs during a 20%, 30%, or even 40% market decline help accelerate your long-term dividend income? What happens if companies cut their dividends? And how does continuing to invest during a crash compare with waiting on the sidelines?

Whether you're investing for retirement, building a passive-income portfolio, or trying to reach financial independence, this video will help you understand the numbers behind investing through market volatility.

The goal isn't to predict the next stock market crash. It's to understand how consistent investing, dividend reinvestment, and long-term compounding can work together through different market conditions.

**COMMENT BELOW:** During a market crash, do you keep buying dividend ETFs, hold your investments, or wait for prices to recover?

WHAT’S NEXT FOR GOLD, SILVER AND STOCKS?

Gold is down about 32% from its January peak, while silver has fallen about 62%. Central banks are buying more gold as investors reassess their exposure to gold and silver ETFs. Meanwhile, the Nifty 50 and Sensex pull back after hitting nearly nine-month highs. How should investors think about diversification as stocks recover and precious metals slide?

Goldman Sachs upgraded Indian equities to overweight and set a Nifty 50 target of 28,500 by the end of 2027, citing strong corporate earnings and domestic demand. Societe Generale plans to set up an equity capital markets business in India as global banks compete for IPO mandates.

The episode also looks at a snag in the India-UK free trade agreement. Bulk Scotch imports reportedly face an effective duty of 162.5%, above the pre-deal rate.

WHAT HAPPENS IF THE AI TRADE LOSES MOMENTUM?

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warns that the global economy is increasingly dependent on AI investment. Circular financing among AI companies has topped $1 trillion, with roughly two-thirds funded by debt. What would a sharp drop in investor confidence mean for financial markets?

WHY ARE FOREIGN INVESTORS RETURNING TO INDIAN STOCKS?

Radhika Rao explains how lower crude oil prices, resilient corporate earnings and a cooling AI trade helped bring foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) back to India. The first wave has favoured large caps and financials. Can the rally broaden if inflation stays elevated and the RBI raises the repo rate?

videos.description:
Welcome back to WHERE U BEANS!? 🌵🚵‍♂️

This week's ride starts in North Phoenix at the Desert Vista Trailhead in the Sonoran Preserve, where I set out to tackle the Dixie Mountain Loop. But a couple of summit signs caught my attention, and naturally, I couldn't resist taking the detours!

What started as a ride through the Sonoran Preserve turned into a challenging adventure featuring two mountain summits, some seriously technical terrain, and even a little spill along the way!

I climbed to the top of Dixie Mountain Summit, a Double Black Diamond challenge, before continuing around the loop and discovering another tempting trail: Western Vista Summit. That one added another steep, technical climb and an exciting descent that made every bit of the effort worthwhile.

THE RIDE STATS: 🚵‍♂️ Location: Sonoran Preserve – North Phoenix, Arizona
📍 Starting Point: Desert Vista Trailhead
⛰️ Trails: Hawk's Nest, Dixie Mountain Loop, Dixie Mountain Summit & Western Vista Summit
📏 Distance: Approximately 7 miles
⬆️ Elevation Gain: 1,237 feet
⬇️ Elevation Loss: 1,237 feet

But as exciting as those summits were, there's a much bigger story behind this week's episode.

Two days after the Sedona Mountain Bike Festival, I was riding my home trails when the unthinkable happened: I finally broke my mountain bike frame.

After three and a half years of riding, thousands upon thousands of miles, and pushing my Rocky Mountain hardtail harder than ever, the original bike that helped build this channel had finally reached a turning point.

I wasn't filming when it happened, but thankfully, I had this ride in the can!

What followed was a week of mixed emotions, searching bike shops, checking out new bikes, and trying to figure out what came next. Then I decided to revisit the shop where I originally purchased my bike. And that's when things took an unexpected turn…

A warranty replacement meant the original hardtail wasn't going away after all!

But that's not the only news. I've also pulled the trigger on something completely different: my first full-suspension mountain bike!

I'm keeping the identity of that new bike under wraps for now. You'll have to stay tuned for the reveal!

In the meantime, I'm officially bike-less, going a little stir-crazy, playing with the dogs, attempting to get some real estate work done, and even dusting off the golf clubs. Let's just say mountain biking is definitely what I prefer doing! 😂

videos.title: Why You Avoid the Things You Actually Love Doing | Carl Jung Psychology
videos.description:
Why do we avoid things we love? If you keep procrastinating on things you love, like the guitar gathering dust or the sketchbook still in its wrapper, Carl Jung’s psychology has a surprising answer. Most procrastination psychology blames laziness or a fear of starting something new, but Jungian psychology and depth psychology suggest the resistance may show how much you care.

This video explores the Carl Jung psychology of avoidance through ten ideas from Jungian psychology and depth psychology. It begins with Jung complexes, the old voices that call a passion a waste of time, and the senex, the inner critic who only hears the wrong notes. Then the puer aeternus and the provisional life Marie-Louise von Franz lectured on, and enantiodromia, the reason resistance can grow right alongside love.

Next comes the ego and Self, and why a numinous pull toward something can feel like a threat. Jung’s transcendent function and his patients’ paintings show how creative work opens a door to the unconscious. Shadow work leads to the golden shadow, the gifts we buried early, and the persona that keeps them out of sight. Finally: vocation, individuation, the circumambulation of the Self, and the wounded healer.

Sources & further reading:

Carl Jung

Memories, Dreams, Reflections
Psychological Types (Collected Works, Vol. 6)
Two Essays on Analytical Psychology (Collected Works, Vol. 7)
The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche (Collected Works, Vol. 8), including “A Review of the Complex Theory” and “The Transcendent Function”
The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (Collected Works, Vol. 9i)
Aion (Collected Works, Vol. 9ii)

The Practice of Psychotherapy (Collected Works, Vol. 16), including “The Aims of Psychotherapy” and “Fundamental Questions of Psychotherapy”
The Development of Personality (Collected Works, Vol. 17)

Other authors

Marie-Louise von Franz, The Problem of the Puer Aeternus (1970)
Robert A. Johnson, Owning Your Own Shadow (1991)
James Hillman, “Senex and Puer” (1967)
Rudolf Otto, The Idea of the Holy (1917)

videos.title: I Gatecrashed a Group Ride! 😂 | UK MTB Trails
videos.description:
Back out on my favourite MTB trails for a bit of solo riding, although it didn't stay that way for long! 😂

Headed up the hill to get a few laps in, dodging the dog muck along the way. Seriously, how difficult is it to clean up after your dog? And it looks like the fly-tippers have been at it round here as well. Some people really don't give a toss, do they?

Anyway, enough moaning. Onto the good stuff!

The trails were running absolutely brilliant. Loads of grip, plenty of speed and a cracking mix of fast, flowing singletrack and the tighter, twistier stuff where you're weaving between trees and picking your way over roots. Just how I like it.

After a few laps on my own, I spotted another couple of groups out riding and decided to gatecrash their ride. 😂 Thankfully they didn't seem to mind me tagging along!

We headed up to some of the lesser-ridden trails and ended up finding another spot I'd not ridden before, complete with a jump line that looks well worth a go.

Didn't ride the jumps this time, but I'll be heading back to give them a try, so keep an eye out for that in another video.

As much as I enjoy getting out for a ride on my own, it's always better when you've got a few others to ride with, have a laugh and discover somewhere new.

Big thanks to the lads for letting me tag along. Really enjoyed it! 👍

The location stays undisclosed, as usual. Some trails are better kept that way.

If you're into UK mountain biking, natural singletrack, fast forest trails and a bit of general messing about on bikes, have a look round the channel.

Cheers for watching, and I'll see you on the next one!

videos.title: Przychody +1127% w rok: ile naprawdę jest warte IPO? | Anthropic AI Analiza Fundamentalna
videos.description:
Anthropic – analiza fundamentalna akcji przed debiutem na giełdzie Nasdaq: przychody +1127% w rok, ale ile wart jest ten potencjał wzrostu przy przedziale 70-78 USD za akcję i co mówi nasza prognoza ceny akcji na koniec 2027 roku? Spółka nie ma jeszcze żadnego raportu finansowego jako firma notowana, więc czytamy prospekt S-1/A linijka po linijce – dla każdego, kto interesuje się inwestowaniem na giełdzie i największym debiutem roku w branży AI.

W tej analizie:
- Jak Claude zamienia tokeny w przychody: 79% za zużycie, 21% subskrypcje
- 55% firmowych wydatków na API modeli językowych (Menlo) i wojna cenowa w AI
- Dlaczego 104 mld USD straty netto to głównie wycena obligacji zamiennych
- Skorygowana marża operacyjna z -93% do +15% w rok
- Portfel kontraktów 13,8 mld USD wobec rocznego tempa przychodów 81 mld USD
- Ok. 1,05 bln USD zobowiązań na moc obliczeniową wobec 212,7 mld USD gotówki pro forma
- Dlaczego nagłówkowe 968 mld USD to po pełnym rozwodnieniu 1,33 bln USD
- Akcjonariat, kontrola założycieli i kalendarz lock-upów
- Mnożniki na tle NVIDII, Microsoftu, Palantira, Cloudflare, ServiceNow i CoreWeave
- Trzy ścieżki przychodów do 2028 roku, ocena 73,7/100 i trzy scenariusze cenowe

Konflikt interesów: kanał AI Inwestuje działa na modelach Claude firmy Anthropic, a tę analizę napisał model Claude. Każda liczba pochodzi z prospektu S-1/A albo z datowanego źródła – oceniajcie wnioski, mając to na uwadze. Akcje nie były jeszcze notowane: każda wartość na akcję odnosi się do przedziału cenowego oferty, a doniesień o nadsubskrypcji spółka nie potwierdziła.

Werdykt rozstrzyga się w 2028 roku: przedział oferty już wycenia scenariusz bazowy, w którym przychody mniej więcej się potrajają, a potencjał ponad to zależy od tego, czy wolumen tokenów wyprzedzi obniżki cen.

Tematy: sztuczna inteligencja, generatywna AI, modele językowe, agenci AI, Claude Code, OpenAI, Google Gemini, centra danych, wycena IPO, debiut na Nasdaq, rozwodnienie akcji, lock-up, spółka pożytku publicznego, obligacje zamienne, marża operacyjna, wolne przepływy pieniężne, koszt kapitału, stopy procentowe, spółki wzrostowe, akcje technologiczne, akcje amerykańskie, inwestowanie długoterminowe.

Więcej spółek z USA na naszym siostrzanym kanale AI Invests. To materiał edukacyjny, a nie porada inwestycyjna; scenariusze to ilustracja, która może okazać się całkowicie błędna.

videos.title: Get Into the Weeds  Jen Farrell and Vitória Suplicy on the Art of Slowing Down and Staying Curious
videos.description:
Travis Heath talks with Drs. Jen Farrell and Vitória Suplicy, who share a private practice in Central Florida that provides therapy and clinical suppervision. They explore the growing trend towards short-term, symptom-focused care, productivity pressures, and clients equipped with social media inspired labels. Their answer is to slow down, ask questions, and stay with discomfort, in therapy and in supervision.

**In this episode**

- [05:04] How they interview new clinicians, and why interventions starting five minutes into a mock intake worried them
- [07:15] Travis's client on whether AI will replace therapists: "they'll only replace the bad ones"
- [09:15] Why newer therapists feel the pressure to fix, and what case conceptualization adds (the tip of the iceberg)
- [12:02] What pushes therapy toward speed: four-to-six-session expectations, symptom measures, caseloads, and notes written for compliance
- [14:19] What clients now expect from therapy, and hearing "this is not what I thought therapy was like"
- [18:46] Slowing down, modeling curiosity, and what to ask when a client says "my ex is a narcissist"
- [21:34] Validation: "aren't you supposed to validate me?" and why it is a start, not the work
- [25:18] Why validating and fixing feel safer than getting curious
- [26:19] What vulnerability actually is, and why trust and time have to come first
- [33:25] How each of them supervises: modeling questions, reading notes, and focusing on process over content
- [38:23] Talking about the relationship with supervisees and clients, and tending to power
- [43:11] Inviting hard conversations into therapy and supervision, and Travis on his early manualized years
- [45:21] Sitting with discomfort and holding environments: "there's beauty and growth in discomfort"
- [48:37] Advice for early-career therapists: go to therapy with someone willing to be curious

Resources & mentions

- Tom Carlson and Sanni Paljakka on "un-stories," the labels clients bring in
- Narrative therapy and Rogerian ideas about the therapeutic relationship, both mentioned by Travis
- Topic pages: [Psychodynamic Psychotherapy](https://www.psychotherapy.net/psychodynamic-psychotherapy/) and [Supervision & Consultation](https://www.psychotherapy.net/supervision-consultation/)
- More from Therapist Confidential and Psychotherapy.net: see Go Deeper

Connect

- Jen Farrell and Vitória Suplicy: Kindness Counseling, kindnesscounseling.net 
- Send your thoughts or experiences: podcast@psychotherapy.

videos.title: Odcinasz się od jednego z rodziców? Powtórzysz jego błędy!
videos.description:
Czy odcięcie od rodziców chroni przed powielaniem ich błędów? No, nie - unikanie trudnych emocji często przynosi odwrotny skutek.

W tym odcinku Podcastu ZOBACZ MNIE rozmawiamy z psychologiem i psychoterapeutą Jackiem Rydlewskim o tym, jak trudne relacje z opiekunami wpływają na nasze dorosłe życie. Często wierzymy, że zerwanie kontaktu to jedyny sposób na wolność, jednak bez przepracowania przeszłości nieświadomie wchodzimy w te same schematy. W tej rozmowie analizujemy, dlaczego prawdziwa separacja emocjonalna wymaga konfrontacji z własnymi lękami, a nie tylko fizycznego dystansu.

Zrozumiesz, jak świadome budowanie własnej tożsamości pozwala wyjść z cienia rodzinnych uwarunkowań. Nasza rozmowa jest przeznaczona dla osób, które czują, że ich przeszłość wciąż definiuje teraźniejszość i szukają zdrowego sposobu na samorozwój. Dowiedz się, jak terapia rodzinna może pomóc w procesie zdrowienia i dlaczego warto zatrzymać destrukcyjne dziedzictwo, zanim przekażesz je dalej.

videos.title: Jeff Hopkins Built a BMX Legacy Nobody Can Forget
videos.description:
# Jeff Hopkins | Nebraska BMX Hall of Fame – From Schwinn Scrambler to BMX Racing Legend

It all started with a Flamboyant Red Schwinn Sting-Ray, a few homemade wooden ramps, and a kid who loved riding his bike. For Jeff Hopkins, that early passion turned into a lifelong connection with BMX racing that continues to this day.

In this special Nebraska BMX Hall of Fame feature, Jeff looks back on his BMX journey, beginning with his very first race in September 1979 at Spinnin’ Spokes in Omaha, Nebraska. Riding a completely stock Schwinn Scrambler with steel wheels and a coaster brake, Jeff crashed during his first practice lap—but somehow still managed to bring home a first-place trophy!

By 1980, Jeff was quickly moving through the ranks, earning his place in the Expert class and competing against some of Nebraska's top young racers at tracks including Spinnin’ Spokes, Gnarlsbad, and the Lincoln YMCA. His competitive career continued to take off in 1981 when he joined Randy’s Cycling Shop as a sponsored rider and began racing nearly every weekend.

Jeff shares memories of competing at tracks throughout Nebraska and Iowa, battling talented riders like Doug Prather and Roger Frakes, earning a high ranking in Iowa District 2, and being named Rider of the Year at River City BMX in Council Bluffs.

He also recalls testing his skills against factory-sponsored riders at national events, including a memorable fourth-place finish in a national main event in Des Moines.

But Jeff's cycling story didn't end when his early BMX racing years were over. He carried his skills into mountain biking and river racing before eventually returning to BMX when his son began racing. He also contributed to early track development and improvements at Omaha BMX at Hefflinger Park.

Today, Jeff still enjoys riding, especially on his 26-inch dirt jumper and single-speed bikes. For him, BMX has never really been something from the past. It's a passion that has followed him throughout his life.

From his first race on a Schwinn Scrambler to competing on the national stage and eventually returning to the sport as a parent and volunteer, Jeff Hopkins represents the lifelong spirit of BMX.

Abi Asija speaks with Michael Swigunski, founder of Dividends Capital, an AI-powered investing platform he is building to help everyday investors gain exposure to established online businesses and their recurring cash flow. A former employee #4 at Empire Flippers, Michael draws on experience in online business acquisitions to pursue a new kind of investment marketplace. Dividends is pre-revenue, and his immediate bottleneck is raising $1 million to build the platform, hire a team, and begin onboarding businesses. At the time of recording, he reports $170,000 raised on Wefunder and another $500,000 in verbal, nonbinding commitments.

Key Insight: A marketplace that promises investors access to business cash flow must do more than raise capital. It has to match realistic valuations with founder incentives, investor return targets, operational oversight, and trust on both sides.

Michael outlines two possible deal structures: partial exits that provide capital to owners who still want to grow their businesses, and full acquisitions that Dividends could operate. The initial focus is recurring-revenue B2B software companies. Abi tests the model with a hypothetical business earning $300,000 in annual profit. If a traditional broker sale might value it at $600,000 to $1.2 million, how can Dividends justify a proposed $3 million valuation while still delivering returns to investors?

The conversation examines earnouts, reinvestment requirements, escrow accounts, and milestones for releasing capital to founders. Michael describes a proposed 8% fee on capital raised for businesses, a 15% share of returns above the investor target, and an 8% to 15% fee if a business exits. Abi challenges whether minority investors and advisors can influence growth when a founder retains majority control, and whether investor payouts remain feasible if the business stays flat. These structures and returns are proposals, not guaranteed outcomes.

They also examine the company's $10 million SAFE valuation cap, Michael's 40,000-person email list, conference outreach to angel investors and VCs, and why winning retail investors' trust may be harder than sourcing owners seeking capital. SHOWNOTES
What happens when a film diagnoses male emotional numbness so accurately that audiences mistake its warning for a cure?

In episode 8-358 of The Films That Made Us, Gunter Swoboda revisits David Fincher's FIGHT CLUB (1999), exploring masculinity, violence, dissociation, satire, and the need for human connection.

After a divisive theatrical release, the film found a second life on DVD, becoming a cultural phenomenon whose influence sometimes obscured its warning.

Gunter examines the narrator's insomnia, consumer-driven life, and inability to name his feelings through normative male alexithymia: how restrictive masculine expectations can make emotional awareness and expression difficult.

In a support group, Bob's embrace offers permission to feel. Tyler Durden instead offers sensation through pain and violence.

Tyler is explored as a metaphor for dissociated parts of the narrator, not a clinical diagnosis. Project Mayhem promises liberation but creates another system of conformity and destruction.

The film's satire can sound sincere to viewers who identify with Tyler's rhetoric. Yet its final gesture—reaching for Marla's hand—points toward connection rather than violence.

• The film's 1999 reception, DVD revival & cultural legacy

• Normative male alexithymia & emotional numbness
• Bob's embrace: contact versus sensation
• Tyler as dissociation metaphor, not diagnosis
• Project Mayhem: rebellion becoming conformity
• Why satire can be mistaken for endorsement
• Grief, recognition & Marla's hand

KEY TAKEAWAYS
• Feeling pain is not the same as feeling connected.
• Emotional numbness can involve difficulty naming feelings.
• Restrictive masculine norms can discourage vulnerability.
• Tyler's promises of freedom reproduce control.
• The film portrays violence's consequences, not a cure.
• Being noticed and understood matters more than performing strength.

In this special Nebraska BMX Hall of Fame feature, 2026 inductee Tyson Jurgens takes us through his incredible BMX journey, from those early bike rides with his dad to becoming one of Nebraska's top BMX racers.

Tyson began racing at Star City BMX around 1999-2000, riding his first Redline Proline equipped with Nuke Proof hubs and Technique cranks. videos.title: Why Japan’s Debt Threatens Global Markets
videos.description:
Japan’s debt is nearly twice the size of its economy. For years, low interest rates made that debt cheaper to carry, while investors around the world borrowed in yen to fund investments abroad. What happens when Japanese government bond yields rise and those investors have to rethink their trades?

In this News Nexus documentary, we follow the money from Tokyo’s bond market to Wall Street, European banks, and the U.S. Treasury market. We explain Japan’s debt-to-GDP ratio, the yen carry trade, and how a shift in Japanese interest rates could affect borrowing costs in other countries.

HOW BIG IS JAPAN’S GOVERNMENT DEBT?

The IMF’s October 2026 World Economic Outlook estimated Japan’s gross government debt at 199.4% of GDP. If you’ve seen figures above 250%, you’re looking at older estimates that used a different method. The accounting changed, but refinancing still matters. When a fixed-rate Japanese government bond comes due, the government can issue a new bond to repay it. If the new bond pays a higher rate, the extra interest cost builds over time as more debt rolls over.

THE YEN CARRY TRADE EXPLAINED

The idea is simple. Borrow yen at a low interest rate, convert it into another currency, and buy an asset that could earn more than the loan costs. A stronger yen can wipe out that gain by making the loan more expensive to repay in dollar terms. When many investors try to exit at once, they can sell shares or bonds and buy back yen, adding to the pressure on both markets.

In August 2024, weak U.S. jobs data helped trigger a global sell-off. The Bank for International Settlements found that investors closing leveraged trades amplified the market moves. By October 30, 2026, the Bank of Japan’s overnight rate target was around 1.25%. That policy rate can influence the yen and the cost of funding these trades.

JAPAN’S AGING POPULATION AND THE TAX BASE

Nearly three in ten people in Japan were 65 or older in June 2026, according to provisional population estimates. A smaller working-age population can slow growth in income taxes and payroll contributions, while demand for pensions, health care, and long-term care rises. We look at how higher productivity, more people joining or staying in the workforce, and changes to public policy could ease that pressure.

videos.title: Trade Deficit vs Trade Surplus Explained: Why Neither is Automatically Good or Bad
videos.description:
Does running a trade deficit mean an economy is losing, while a trade surplus means it's winning? The answer is far more surprising than the headlines suggest.

After reading Chapter 10,  The International Trade and Capital Flows, in the free OpenStax Macroeconomics textbook, watch this video to reinforce the important concepts covered in the reading materials.

In this video, we break down international trade and capital flows to explore why trade deficits aren't necessarily bad and surpluses aren't always good. You'll discover how the balance of trade is tied directly to global money flows, moving beyond physical merchandise to look at the complete current account balance—including goods, rapidly growing service exports, income payments, and unilateral transfers.

Using clear economic principles, we unpack the national saving and investment identity to show why a nation's trade balance is driven by its domestic saving, investment, and government borrowing rather than trade barriers or specific industries. Through real-world historical examples—ranging from 19th-century America and 1970s South Korea to financial crises in Latin America and East Asia—you'll see when borrowing from abroad fuels long-term economic growth and when sudden capital flight creates serious vulnerabilities.

⭐ In This Video, You'll Learn: • The difference between the merchandise trade balance and the current account balance • The four components of the current account: goods, services, income payments, and unilateral transfers • Why trade flows are financial flows connecting international trade to global investment • How the national saving and investment identity explains trade imbalances • Why government budget deficits and economic booms tend to widen trade deficits • How foreign borrowing helped build America's 19th-century infrastructure • Why trade surpluses do not guarantee rapid economic growth • The key differences between the overall level of trade and the balance of trade

videos.title: Beyond Survival: Healing Childhood Trauma, Reclaiming Your Worth, and Living a Life You Love
videos.description:
What happens when the experiences that shaped your childhood continue to influence your relationships, emotions, and sense of self decades later? And how do you move beyond simply surviving to create a life you genuinely love?

In this deeply personal episode of the Scars to Stars® Podcast, Deana Brown Mitchell welcomes Nicole LeMaster, a trauma therapist, Somatic Experiencing practitioner, nervous system specialist, and dream coach who helps people navigate trauma and reconnect with their authentic selves.

Nicole courageously shares her journey through childhood trauma, family dysfunction, sexual abuse, and leaving home at just 15 years old. She explores how generational trauma can shape entire families, why siblings often experience the same childhood differently, and how healing can sometimes create distance from people who are not ready to begin their own journeys.

Drawing from her personal experiences and professional work, Nicole explains the connection between trauma, nervous system regulation, emotional responses, and self-worth. She discusses how Somatic Experiencing transformed her own healing process and helped her develop greater self-trust, compassion, and the ability to recognize when her body was responding to past experiences rather than present circumstances.

Deana and Nicole also share a meaningful conversation about suicide, silence, and the healing power of storytelling. Deana reflects on her own suicide attempt, the 23 years she spent keeping that experience private, and how losing a friend ultimately inspired her to speak openly and create the Realize Foundation.

Nicole introduces her workbook, WTF Am I Even Doing?, which combines nervous system education, yoga, reflection, and experiential exercises to help readers explore mind-body alignment and develop a deeper understanding of themselves.

Together, they offer practical insights into recognizing unhealthy patterns, seeking support, establishing boundaries, practicing self-compassion, and reconnecting with the person you truly are.
At the heart of this conversation is a powerful reminder: your past may have shaped your survival, but it does not have to determine your future. Healing creates the possibility of moving beyond survival and building a life filled with authenticity, connection, and purpose.
